title: Mars-surface solar particle events: the RAD team's nowcast rule replayed on MSL RAD (CCMC iSWA)

source.publisher: NASA GSFC Community Coordinated Modeling Center (CCMC), iSWA HAPI server
source.name: MSL RAD Dosimetry dose_e_total, whole surface record (iSWA HAPI id 'msl_rad_dosimetry'), replayed through the nowcast rule of Löwe et al. 2025
source.license: No license or data-use terms stated in the HAPI /info response (checked 2026-11-14).
source.citation: NASA GSFC Community Coordinated Modeling Center (CCMC), Integrated Space Weather Analysis system (iSWA), HAPI dataset 'msl_rad_dosimetry' ('MSL RAD Dosimetry'), parameter dose_e_total, 2012-08-17T00:00:00Z to 2026-11-13T00:00:00Z (pinned), HAPI server https://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/IswaSystemWebApp/hapi, retrieved 2026-11-15T01:19:32Z. Event rule: Löwe JL et al., Nowcasting Solar Energetic Particle Events for Mars Missions, Space Weather 23, e2025SW004372 (2025), doi:10.1029/2025SW004372; numbers from arXiv:2502.02469v1.

caveats: Not reproduced (no sample above 1.25 x background within 48 h of the listed date): 2013-04-10 (max 1.24 x; median spacing 61.6 min); 2013-10-10 (max 1.02 x; iSWA gap: 9 samples on 2013-10-11, 0 samples on 2013-10-12); 2014-09-10 (max 1.16 x); 2023-03-12 (max 1.10 x; iSWA gap: 8 samples on 2023-03-11).
Deviation: 2014-09-02 reproduces at -33% total SEP dose (84.15 uGy against the paper's 125.93 uGy).
2014-01-05: the paper lists this event as not triggered, and the replay agrees: one sample at 2014-01-06T12:45:21Z reached 1.251 x background and the next did not confirm it.
For 2024-07-22, 2024-09-02 the replay's onset falls on a later UTC day (25.1 h, 33.5 h after 00:00 UTC of the listed date); Table 1 prints dates only.

The iSWA record has 22 gaps longer than 2 days (data.record.gaps_over_2_days); the longest runs from 2012-08-18T11:41:51Z to 2013-03-22T04:34:39Z (215.7 days). A storm inside a gap cannot be seen by this replay.
Shelter time of 2024-05-20: 02d 00h:23m in this replay against the paper's 01d 17h:55m; total SEP dose 1745.16 against 1730.55 uGy.
The 2024-05-20 peak ratio (59.7 x) is measured against that event's own 5-day background (140.4 uGy/day); a lower background raises the ratio as much as a higher peak does.

iSWA's cadence (median spacing 17.1 min over the record) differs from the paper's 15-minute PDS product (RAD's 15-minute dose rate data products, archived in NASA's Planetary Data System), so onsets, peaks and ends fall on different samples.

The paper's appendix Table 4 prints a partly different list of surface dates (2014-08-31, 2023-05-19, 2024-10-09 appear there and not in Table 1; 2014-09-02, 2024-05-20, 2024-09-05 appear in Table 1 and not there). This replay uses Table 1 only.

The publisher's description does not say whether dose_e_total is RTG-corrected. On the rover's RTG background, the paper (Löwe et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.02469v1, appendix) writes: "Dose rate E is not affected by the additional radiation from radioactive decay, as its detection threshold is sufficiently high to exclude the RTG background. In contrast, the measurements of dose rate B include the RTG background." The rule's ratios are taken as served.
Absorbed dose in plastic: never converted to Sv, never compared with Table 4.8-1.
Numbers from arXiv:2502.02469v1 Table 1 (Martian surface); the journal version (doi:10.1029/2025SW004372) was not compared.

Whole-record scan: 13 triggers. Those that match no row of the paper's table are listed as triggers not in the paper's table: this replay does not decide whether they were SEP events. Triggers after the paper's surface record ends (2024-09-09) are listed with any DONKI entries logged near them, which are not claimed to be the same event.
Earth timings are lower bounds from light time only (JPL Horizons one-way light time at 00:00 UTC that day): no ground processing, relay or link schedule is added.

data.explainer: The SEP nowcast rule the MSL RAD team published (Löwe et al. 2025), run on the whole public record of Curiosity's dose rate on the surface of Mars and compared row by row with the paper's own Table 1. A replay of a measured record: nothing here feeds LANDFALL's engine, rules or scenario.

dataset.description: Radiation dose rate in tissue-equivalent plastic detector E
dataset.title: MSL RAD Dosimetry

pre_record_probe.basis: every window from the dataset's startDate (floored to the day) to the pinned start returned HAPI 1406 'No data available'

method: Background = arithmetic mean of E over the 5 UTC days before the event day (a least-squares constant fit equals the mean of the points).

Onset = first sample above 1.25 x background within 2 days of 00:00 UTC on the date whose next sample, less than 3 h later, is above too: that next sample is the paper's cross-check (its case 2), and the 3 h limit is the whole-record scan's design choice. A sample the next one does not confirm is not an onset. End = first later sample below the threshold.

Total SEP dose = trapezoid of (E - background) from onset to end, in uGy; time to peak and lead time are measured from the onset sample; lead time ends at the first sample at which 10% of the total has accumulated (sample resolution).

scan.method: Background refit each UTC day from the 5 UTC days before it (at least 100 samples) and frozen during an event; a trigger needs two consecutive samples above the threshold less than 3 h apart.

source.rationale: LANDFALL's own limits for running the rule on iSWA's uneven cadence: at least 100 samples in the 5-day background, and a confirming sample less than 3 h after the first.
What counts as reproducing a row: total SEP dose within 15% and time to peak within 40 min of the paper.

literature.title: Nowcasting Solar Energetic Particle Events for Mars Missions
literature.numbers_from: arXiv:2502.02469v1 Table 1 (Martian surface); the journal version was not compared

quotes.text: We apply a constant linear fit to the dose rate E measured in 15-minute cadences over the five days preceding the SEP event.
An SEP event is considered triggered when the dose rate exceeds the background level by more than 25%, corresponding to a threshold of 1.25 times the background dose rate.
A consecutive measurement is then used as a cross-check to verify or falsify the SEP event.
In the second case, two consecutive measurements must exceed the threshold.
the astronaut will receive an official alert
The end of an SEP event is defined when the dose rate E drops below the 25% trigger threshold.
Therefore, the 'shelter duration' is the time calculated from onset to end of the SEP event.
For this time period, we calculate the background-removed accumulated SEP dose, referred to as the 'total SEP dose' (see Figure 3, right).
The shelter duration is the time from onset to end of the SEP event, and the time to peak is the time from onset to the maximum of dose rate E.

The lead time is defined as the period in which an astronaut can avoid at least 90% of the total SEP dose (time region marked in red) and would receive only 10% of the total SEP dose (time region marked in orange).

Our study suggests that, using our nowcasting system, an astronaut should not move more than 30 minutes away from a shelter in order to still avoid not only more than 90% of the total SEP dose but also the peak dose rate in the case of an SEP event.
Four SEP events on the surface of Mars do not exceed the 25% trigger threshold and therefore cannot be identified using our methodology.
on the Martian surface from landing on August 6, 2012, to September 9, 2024
Alongside the 15-minute dose rate data products, RAD also provides high-resolution dose rate measurements as one-minute data products.
The data used in this study are archived in the NASA Planetary Data System's Planetary Plasma Interactions Node at the University of California, Los Angeles.
